subject: knitr: xtable disrupts code chunks after the table

messages.author: 3094c578142f6921
messages.subject: knitr: xtable disrupts code chunks after the table
parts:
As best as I can tell, the Rmd file compiles to md correctly, but then the html file output gets a bit squirrely - any code chunks after the xtable() chunk are not formatted correctly. 

Here is my Rmd file: 

Weird xtable problems
========================================================
Xtable works as it should
```{r xtablechunk, results='asis'}
data(iris)
library(xtable)
print(xtable(head(iris)), type='html')
```

Any code chunks after xtable are a bit weird

```{r stargazer, results='asis', message=F}
library(stargazer)
model <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Petal.Length, data=iris)
stargazer(model, type="html", summary=F)
```

The stargazer code works fine if the xtable chunk is removed. 

Any ideas?

messages.author: 889de486273d901d
messages.subject: Re: knitr: xtable disrupts code chunks after the table
parts:
Perhaps a bug in the markdown package rather than in knitr.   At least the .md intermediate file looks ok to me.   

In any case if I remove the three spaces before the first </TABLE> it will render fine.  I have no idea why that gives the 
markdownToHTML() function indigestion, but eliminating those leading spaces before the table close seems to fix the problem.

Commands I used to generate were,

knitr::knit("star.Rmd")
markdownToHTML("star.md", "star.html", options=c("use_xhtml"))

and I see the problem 










FWIW, this does not occur when using the new rmarkdown() package

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: knitr: xtable disrupts code chunks after the table
parts:
Thanks Chris. You are right -- it is a bug of the markdown package
(actually a bug of sundown, the rendering engine behind markdown). The
problem was caused by the indentation of

</TABLE>

I'd also recommend testing the new rmarkdown package:
http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/ The new rendering engine, Pandoc, is way
stronger than sundown.

Regards,
Yihui
